assumptions: Invented educational values, not NASA hardware specifications. One-minute resource preview, preset orbit opportunities, full initial battery. Power margin uses a conservative simultaneous-load design rule. No real trajectory/coverage/lifetime validation yet.

scenario.name: Flood Watch
scenario.baseline_description: Structure, computer, attitude control and storage are included in the fixed bus. Ground-service cost covers the selected 12-month teaching scenario.

options.label: Basic
options.name: Basic imager
options.description: Standard detail with lower power demand and data production.

options.label: Advanced
options.name: Advanced imager
options.description: More detail, but twice the data rate and higher mass, power and cost.

options.label: Compact
options.name: Compact power
options.description: Light solar panels and a small battery leave less reserve.

options.label: Extended
options.name: Extended power
options.description: Larger panels and battery improve power and endurance, but add mass and cost.

options.label: Standard
options.name: Standard radio
options.description: A light radio saves power and money, but transfers less data per contact.

options.label: Fast
options.name: Fast radio
options.description: More data can reach Earth during contact, at a higher power, mass and cost.

options.label: Regional
options.name: Regional orbit preset
options.description: This teaching preset offers ten observing minutes and six contact minutes per cycle.

options.label: Wide
options.name: Wide orbit preset
options.description: More observing time, but longer eclipse, shorter contact and higher ground-service cost.

options.label: Light
options.name: Light launch
options.description: A lower-cost launch supports up to 70 kg to the regional preset only.

options.label: Heavy
options.name: Heavy launch
options.description: A higher-cost launch supports both presets and more spacecraft mass.
